title: One, holy, catholic, apostolic (CCC 811)
hook: the four marks in the Creed

segments.voice: Yesterday, the body of Christ, soma christou: many members, one body, with Christ as head. Your line was many members, one body. Today, four words that describe that body, said every Sunday.

Every Sunday, in churches from Manila to Lagos to Chicago, a whole congregation stands and says the Creed. Near the end comes a line that's easy to rush: I believe in one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church. Four adjectives in a single breath. The words go back to a council of bishops at Constantinople, and Orthodox and some Protestant Christians say them too, each understanding them in their own way. Catholics call them the four marks: the signs by which the Church is recognized. Today, slowly, one word at a time.
screen: `MANILA, LAGOS, CHICAGO.` → `FOUR WORDS IN ONE BREATH.` → `A COUNCIL AT CONSTANTINOPLE.`

segments.voice: One. Paul writes, in the Douay-Rheims: "One Lord, one faith, one baptism." The Catechism says the Church is one because its source is one God, its founder one Christ, its soul one Spirit. One doesn't mean identical. It means one faith, one set of sacraments, one line of shepherds, holding many languages and cultures together. Holy. People sometimes laugh at this one, and the Church admits why: it's full of sinners, and has been from the start. The Catechism says the Church is holy not because its members are, but because Christ made it his own and gives it the means of holiness. It also says, frankly, that the Church is at once holy and always in need of purification. Catholic. It's a Greek word, katholikos, from kath' holou: according to the whole. It means universal, and also whole, nothing missing. The Catechism quotes Ignatius of Antioch, a bishop who wrote, tradition says, on his way to martyrdom in Rome: where Christ Jesus is, there is the catholic Church. Apostolic. The Church is built on the apostles, keeps their teaching, and, Catholics say, is led by bishops who succeed them, in a line of laying on of hands going back to the beginning. So the four marks aren't four boasts. Catholics understand them as gifts from Christ and as tasks: to become more fully one, more holy, more truly whole, and more faithful to what the apostles handed on.
screen: `ONE LORD, ONE FAITH, ONE BAPTISM.` · `HOLY, AND NEEDING PURIFICATION.` · `KATH' HOLOU: ACCORDING TO THE WHOLE.` · `BUILT ON THE APOSTLES.` · then, large: `ONE, HOLY, CATHOLIC, APOSTOLIC.`

segments.voice: Say the four words on four slow breaths out: one, thinking of everyone saying it with you around the world; holy, thinking of one person whose goodness you've seen up close; catholic, picturing the whole, every language, every century; apostolic, thinking of the people who handed faith down to you, or to someone you love. Four breaths, four words, repeated until the bell.
Katholikos, the Greek root of catholic: universal, and whole, nothing missing. One of the Church's four marks in the Creed. Today's word.
Your line: four marks. One, holy, catholic, apostolic: four words, said in one breath every Sunday. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics profess the four marks every Sunday and on solemnities in the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed, which is also said, with differences of understanding, by Orthodox and some Protestant churches.
